No—under those conditions, you would almost certainly **not** be able to see the Moon with normal unaided eyesight.

Although it is geometrically above the horizon, it is:

- only **0.09% illuminated**, an extraordinarily thin crescent,
- just **3.45° from the Sun**, so it is buried in intense daylight glare,
- only about **10.5° above the horizon**, where atmospheric scattering and extinction are strong,
- and apparently just before new Moon.

That combination makes naked-eye detection effectively impossible. Even attempting to locate it with binoculars or a telescope would be unsafe because of its proximity to the Sun. So for practical visual purposes, you can regard the Moon as **not visible** at that time and place.
